case.source_text:
Synthetic nurse note for software testing. No real patient data.

At a commercial-driver reassessment, the driver brings incomplete records from several appointments and says he has recently been more tired on long shifts, with intermittent blur, difficulty following radio instructions and one episode he calls a brief blank moment; his partner describes him stopping mid-sentence, but he remembers remaining upright and denies a definite blackout. The event followed a missed meal, yet no glucose was measured before he ate and a later result of 7.0 mmol/L does not establish what happened during the episode.

He reports established diabetes and a recently introduced injection whose name he cannot recall, while an older list still describes tablet treatment only. BP 176/100 mmHg was recorded immediately after arrival and BP 150/88 mmHg after rest; a note mentioning persistent hypertension predates a medication change, and no recent home log or assessment of treatment-related dizziness is available.

An eye screening lists right 6/12 and left 6/9 without correction status, and a hearing sheet gives 44 dB without identifying an ear or the frequencies used; he says the visual blur comes and goes and that the hearing aid was worn for part of the assessment. Current optometry, audiology and specialist medical reports have been requested, and the nurse has not inferred a single cause linking the symptoms or treated the incomplete measurements as verified standards.
